macro: This is a company-specific earnings and news digest for Wednesday, September 30, 2026, covering BMO reporters and pre-market catalysts. No broad index or overnight macro commentary is provided in this edition. Risk tone must be inferred from the individual company results, which are mixed overall.
market_outlook: No explicit directional market call is made in this edition. The earnings slate is mixed — JBL and CAG beat on earnings but guidance nuances temper enthusiasm, while CALM is a clear drag. AI-linked names remain under a high-bar scrutiny lens per Adam's note on JBL.
bull_case: CAG posted a significant EPS beat driven by strong margin execution, suggesting cost-control turnaround efforts are working. JBL delivered massive top-line and EPS upside with bullish forward guidance in its AI-linked Intelligent Infrastructure segment. HPE raised its Networking segment growth outlook and increased Juniper synergy targets meaningfully. CI reaffirmed guidance and issued a 10-14% EPS CAGR target through 2030, implying upside to consensus.
bear_case: CALM reported a brutal quarter with a large EPS miss and a 41.5% revenue collapse, suspending its dividend entirely for the period. FDS offered slightly below-consensus F27 guidance on both organic ASV growth and EPS, which Adam flags as likely to pressure the stock. CAG's strong FQ1 beat was not rolled into full-year guidance, signaling a softer outlook for the remaining three quarters. The bar for AI-linked names like JBL remains extremely high, meaning even large headline beats may be treated as merely inline by the market.

company_items.summary: Apple will launch a new smart home device on October 13, marking its entry into a category the company views as strategically critical. This is a long-anticipated product designed to expand Apple's ecosystem footprint into the home. The launch date is now confirmed, giving investors a concrete catalyst to watch.

Conagra beat FQ1 EPS handily at 41 cents versus the Street's 29 cents, with adjusted operating margins of 11.5% crushing the 9.2% estimate. Sales were roughly inline with organic revenue down 1.1% versus the expected negative 1.3%. However, full-year guidance was left unchanged, implying the beat will not carry forward and that FQ2 through FQ4 face a softer outlook.

Cal-Maine posted a deeply disappointing FQ1 with EPS of negative $1.26 versus the Street's negative $0.77 estimate, and revenue collapsed 41.5% to $539 million versus the $552 million consensus. Conventional egg sales fell nearly 60% year-over-year with a negative 35.2% operating margin, the core driver of the disaster. Because EPS was negative, the company's variable dividend policy means no dividend will be paid this quarter.

Cigna reaffirmed its 2026 full-year guidance and issued a long-term financial target of 10 to 14% EPS CAGR through 2030. Using the midpoint of 12% growth off $30.45 in 2026 EPS implies 2030 EPS of roughly $48, which is above the current Street consensus of $45.82. The reaffirmation and above-consensus long-term target provide a modest positive catalyst.

FactSet beat FQ4 EPS by delivering $4.52 versus the $4.37 estimate, up 11.6%, with organic revenue growth of 7.1% topping the 5.75% estimate. However, operating margins contracted 80 basis points year-over-year to 33% due to higher compensation and technology costs. F27 guidance midpoints disappointed on both organic ASV growth at 5.75% versus the 6% consensus and EPS at $19.45 versus $19.76, which Adam says will likely pressure the stock.

General Mills announced a CEO transition effective January 1, 2027, with COO Dana McNabb succeeding Jeff Harmening as Chief Executive Officer. Harmening will move to the role of Executive Chair of the Board. The leadership change is a known transition from within the existing management team.

HPE raised its F27 Networking segment revenue growth guidance to high teens to low 20% year-over-year, up from the prior 14 to 17% range. Juniper integration cost synergy targets were also raised to $800 million from the prior floor of at least $600 million. Data Center Networking revenue is expected to achieve a low-to-high 50% CAGR through F29, a notably aggressive long-term outlook.

Hormel announced the acquisition of Brakebush Brothers, a leading value-added chicken producer, from the Brakebush family for $1.055 billion. The deal is expected to be accretive to adjusted EPS beginning in fiscal year 2028. This represents a meaningful strategic expansion into the value-added poultry category.

Jabil crushed FQ4 estimates with EPS of $4.40 versus $4.07 and revenue of $10.6 billion versus the $9.7 billion estimate, while FQ1 and full F27 guidance midpoints are well above consensus on both EPS and revenue. The Intelligent Infrastructure segment — the AI-linked business — grew 56% to $5.85 billion but margins at 6.5% came in just below the 6.65% estimate. Adam cautions that the bar for AI names is very high and what looks like a massive beat on paper may ultimately be treated as merely inline.

Norwegian Cruise Line said Q3 results will come in ahead of prior guidance while its full 2026 outlook is affirmed. This is the second positive cruise industry data point in two days, following Carnival's encouraging report on Tuesday. The read-through suggests continued resilience in consumer demand for cruise travel.

sectors: Cruise sector showing back-to-back positive data points with both Carnival and Norwegian flagging better-than-expected results, suggesting sustained consumer demand. AI infrastructure and networking remain high-bar trades where even large beats may not move stocks meaningfully to the upside. Egg and agricultural commodity names face ongoing pricing headwinds.

Good morning. Here is your briefing for Wednesday, September 30th. This morning's newsletter is a pure earnings and company news edition — there is no fresh macro commentary or index-level directional call from Adam today, so let's go straight to the names.

Starting with Apple. The company confirmed it will launch its new smart home device on October 13th. This is a long-anticipated product in a category Apple considers strategically critical. The launch date is now locked in — clean bullish catalyst.

Conagra delivered a strong fiscal first quarter earnings beat — 41 cents versus the Street at 29 cents — driven by adjusted operating margins of 11.5% against a 9.2% estimate. Sales were roughly inline. The problem: full-year guidance was left unchanged. Adam's read is that the beat doesn't carry forward, implying a softer second through fourth quarter outlook. Mixed signal.

Cal-Maine is the ugly one this morning. EPS came in at negative $1.26 versus the Street's negative 77 cents. Revenue crashed 41.5% to $539 million. Conventional egg sales collapsed nearly 60% year-over-year with a negative 35.2% operating margin. And because EPS was negative, the variable dividend gets suspended entirely. Clearly bearish.

Cigna reaffirmed 2026 guidance and laid out a 10 to 14% earnings per share compound annual growth rate target through 2030. The midpoint implies 2030 EPS of roughly $48, which beats the Street's $45.82 consensus. Modest positive.

FactSet beat fiscal fourth quarter EPS at $4.52 versus $4.37 and posted 7.1% organic revenue growth versus a 5.75% estimate. But fiscal 2027 guidance midpoints on both organic ASV growth and EPS came in slightly below consensus. Adam flags this guidance shortfall as the likely driver of downward pressure on the stock today.

HP Enterprise raised its fiscal 2027 Networking segment revenue growth guidance to high teens to low 20% year-over-year, up from 14 to 17%. Juniper synergy targets moved to $800 million from the prior floor of $600 million. Data Center Networking is targeting a low-to-high 50% compound annual growth rate through fiscal 2029. Clearly bullish.

Jabil is the most nuanced read this morning. The company blew past fiscal fourth quarter estimates — $4.40 EPS versus $4.07, revenue of $10.6 billion versus $9.7 billion — and forward guidance on both fiscal first quarter and full fiscal 2027 is well above the Street. The Intelligent Infrastructure AI segment grew 56% to $5.85 billion. But Adam's key point: the bar for AI-linked names is extremely high. A massive beat on paper may simply register as inline in the market's eyes. Watch the price action carefully.

Hormel announced a $1.055 billion acquisition of Brakebush Brothers, a value-added chicken company, expected to be earnings per share accretive starting in fiscal 2028. And Norwegian Cruise Line said third quarter results will beat prior guidance with the full 2026 outlook affirmed — the second positive cruise print in two days after Carnival reported Tuesday.

Bottom line for today: the tape is mixed. You have genuine strength in AI infrastructure names and cruise, an ugly agricultural read from Cal-Maine, and a nuanced set of beats where guidance or quality of the beat matters more than the headline number. AI names in particular trade on a high bar — do not chase the Jabil headline without watching how the market actually responds at the open.
